Hi Lauren,

We've attached our benchmark_spec_v1 (spreadsheet) with target load shapes.

- Your recommended test harness and configs so we can reproduce runs in our environment
- Clear definitions of metrics you will report (including how you calculate p95/p99 across requests vs tokens)
- Baseline numbers on dedicated vs hosted modes for a 2k-token average request (if possible) and how batching/kv-cache changes results
- Any side effects (e.g., memory growth, cache invalidation windows) and recommended guardrails

Can you confirm Redwood can run a vendor-observed live validation during our procurement window (target week of Jan 18)? Also include any required SLAs or constraints for Dedicated capacity.

Appreciate a single consolidated response we can include in the RFP appendix.

Best,
Alex

Alex —

Thanks — attached is our detailed performance questionnaire (redwood_performance_q_v3.pdf) and a proposed mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan.docx). High level answers below; the attached doc enumerates full methodology and suggested measurement scripts.

Summary (short):
- Test harness: we recommend using our open-source workload-generator (links + runbook in the PDF). For reproducibility we publish a dockerized harness that drives the Redwood API and emits both per-request and per-token telemetry.
- Metrics we report: p50/p95/p99 latency (per request), token throughput (tokens/sec), completion time distribution, warm vs steady-state comparisons, and resource utilization (GPU %, memory, PCIe bandwidth). We explicitly state measurement window and sample sizes.
- Baselines: for a 2k-token average prompt on a Dedicated 8xA10G pool we typically see sustained token throughput ~9,000–12,000 tokens/sec with median latency ~120ms (per request) under steady-state batching at 256-token batch window. Hosted (shared) numbers are 30–40% higher latency variability; we include an anonymized run sheet in the PDF.
- Batching & KV cache: enabling KV cache for repeated context reduces effective latency by up to 45% for refactored prompts; batching helps throughput but increases p50 by batching-window ms. Our doc shows tradeoff curves and recommended batch sizes by sequence-length distribution.
- Failure modes: cache eviction patterns can spike tail latency during cache misses and model evictions; we recommend a 10–15 minute pre-warm period and a ramp policy for sudden bursts.

Operational asks from Orion:
1) Provide the workload CSV (we saw the attached spec — thanks).
2) Give us a test account or safe sample tokens to run the harness against (we can run in our lab or give you an invite to a vendor-observed run in our Dedicated lab).
3) Confirm desired SLAs (p95 target, monthly thresholds) so we can size Dedicated capacity and reserve slots for your window.

Proposed next steps (included in the MAP):
- Jan 12: exchange NDA/test-account details
- Jan 14: technical kickoff with Rishi (runtime lead) to align on harness config
- Jan 18: two vendor-observed runs (steady-state + spike) with live telemetry and a follow-up results deck

I copied Rishi and Marissa for technical and contract follow-up. We can tweak the plan to match your procurement timeline.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_performance_q_v3.pdf, mutual_action_plan.docx

Alex / team —

Quick technical clarifications to make the live runs reproducible:
- Hardware variants: we typically run Dedicated experiments on AWS G5/4/5g-equivalent (A10G, A100 where applicable). Please let us know which instance family you prefer. Numbers in the PDF are from 8xA10G.
- Sequence lengths: please include the empirical distribution (we need mean, median, 90th percentile tokens). The harness supports per-request sequence sampling and replay to mimic real traffic.
- Measurement windows: we recommend a 15m warmup, 30m steady-state window, and 5x spike windows (10s bursts) to capture tail behavior. All latencies are measured at the request boundary (end-to-end, including queuing). Token-level timings are also emitted.
- Batching policy: our runtime supports continuous batching. For reproducibility set explicit batch target (e.g., 64/128/256) and max latency budget for the batch. The harness will surface per-batch sizes and timing.
- Consistency: for p99 we report the empirical endpoint across all requests in the measurement window (not averaged across hosts). If you prefer aggregation per host then the numbers can differ — call out which you want in the spec.
- Observability: we can provide a temporary Redwood Console view with token-level traces and a Grafana dashboard for the run. We will also export raw telemetry (ndjson) if Orion's analytics team wants to ingest.

Attaching a short checklist in the PDF describing toggles that materially affect results (quantization profile, KV cache enabled, model variant, sequence padding strategy).

Rishi
Principal Architect, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference
